changes: p1: as_written now has the fuller line as R. reads it, 'paunapānyā bhikṣuṇī'. Name changed from the placeholder 'Unknown' to the tentative reading 'Paunapānī', based on R.'s 'paunapānyā'. Confidence stays low.
p1 evidence now quotes the donation formula 'bhikṣuṇī ... svayam dattā eṣā śilādroṇī'.
Place as_written now names the full find-spot, 'Lalitpur (Patan), Bhwanginani-tole Water-reservoir'.
Notes expanded: they now give both editors' readings, the metre problem, and that no date is visible.

purpose: Records that a Buddhist nun (bhikṣuṇī) donated a stone water conduit or basin (śilādroṇī) for the welfare of all living beings (sattvānāṃ hitahetave)
notes: The donor's name is damaged. R. reads 'paunapānyā bhikṣuṇī', which may be an oblique form of a personal name such as Paunapānī. DV reads only 'ḥ paun - - mbhikṣuṇī su--kyā', and their 'su--kyā' could be part of the name or an epithet. The verse is an anuṣṭubh, but R.'s first pāda has only 7 syllables, so R.'s text is probably corrupt there too. The name is therefore uncertain and should not be relied on. The editor reports that no date is visible. Concordance: DV 181; Gn LXXXVI; HJ 158; R. 153. The site lies at the eastern edge of Patan.
